This paper proposes a multi-specialty collaborative design method based on unified modeling of multi-source data, which will conduct unified modeling of heterogeneous data involving multiple specialties and various software tools, and uniformly invoke according to the data requirements of design tools, so as to realize unified invocation and control of multi-specialty design data in the whole life cycle. The inconsistencies of heterogeneous data in the design process are effectively solved, and the design efficiency and quality are improved.

articleTitle: A Classification Method of Magnetic Flux Leakage Signal for Internal and External Wall Defects in Seamless Steel Pipes Based on Spectrogram and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Magnetic flux leakage non-destructive testing is an important method for comprehensive inspection of seamless steel pipes. Distinguishing the signals formed by internal and external wall defects is a significant issue in this method. This study proposes a new approach, which first converts the magnetic flux leakage signal obtained by the sensors into a spectrogram and calculates its gray level co-occurrence matrix. Then, it calculates the energy, entropy, and correlation at four different angles of the matrix. The mean and standard deviation of these quantities are used as the characteristic values of the defect signal. Combining with support vector machine technology, an identification model for the signals of internal and external wall defects is established. The model processes the test signal to achieve automatic defect classification. Experimental results show that this method can effectively identify and classify defect signals with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Fusion Algorithm for Path Planning based on Improved A* and Ant Colony
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of slow convergence speed and easy to fall into local optimal solutions in the application of ant colony algorithm for path planning, a path planning fusion algorithm based on improved A* and ant colony is proposed. Firstly, the A* algorithm is improved by introducing a dynamic weighting factor Q to improve the search speed of the algorithm; then, the improved A* algorithm is utilized for path preplanning, and the regional pheromone concentration of the ant colony algorithm is redistributed to reduce the convergence time of the ant colony and to improve the path search efficiency; secondly, a new weight function is added and the transfer probability of the ant colony is improved to reduce the blindness of the transfer and the number of iterations; and finally. Three times B-splines are introduced to optimize the smoothness of the path. Analyzed by MATLAB simulation in the map set in the paper, the fusion algorithm reduces the length of the optimal path by 5.96%, the number of iterations by 34.42%, and the average time consumed by 4.47% compared with the traditional ant colony algorithm.

articleTitle: Application of the Logistic Regression Algorithm for the Diagnosis of Stomach Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Logistic regression is a widely utilized machine learning algorithm for binary classification tasks. In this study, the logistic regression algorithm is used to classify whether a disorder can be diagnosed as a stomach disease. The levels of four test indicators, ceruloplasmin, blue reaction, indole-acetic acid, and neutral sulfides, are considered as features. Eleven data sets in the training set and four data sets in the testing set are employed. The data sets have been desensitized. The predicted classifications for the testing set align with the true classifications. Feature importance analysis is also performed. The first three test indicators significantly influence classification, each contributing an average of over 30%, whereas the neutral sulfides level has minimal impact, accounting for less than 1%. Therefore, the level of neutral sulfides alone is not regarded as a key indicator for diagnosing stomach disease. This study not only offers insights for clinical diagnosis but also highlights the potential of machine learning algorithms in medical applications.

articleTitle: A Resource Allocation Strategy for Virtual Power Plants Based on URLLC to Minimize Control Costs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: With the swift growth of renewable energy and the evolution of smart grid technologies, the concept of the Virtual Power Plant (VPP) has risen as a pioneering strategy for energy management, marking a pivotal area of study within power system research. Nonetheless, the effectiveness of VPPs hinges on the implementation of Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communications (URLLC). In VPP operations, communication lags or data packet losses can result in the delayed or failed execution of control instructions, impacting both the stability of the electrical grid and the efficacy of energy management. Against this backdrop, this paper aims to bolster the control capabilities of VPPs by integrating control demands with URLLC constraints. We have crafted an optimization problem designed to reduce control expenditures in VPP operations through strategic distribution of potential data packet losses and wireless resources, all the while guaranteeing the stability of the power grid and the productivity of energy transactions. To tackle this issue, we have developed a Greedy Choice-Local Search Strategy algorithm (GC-LSS) that seeks to achieve the lowest possible control costs within the bounds of communication constraints. The simulation outcomes align with the expected parameter variations, and our proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to random allocation methods.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of "Cloud + Edge"Meteorological Blockchain Distributed Storage and Network Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: This paper studies a blockchain-based solution for the distributed storage and networking of meteorological data, aiming to address issues in traditional meteorological data storage and transmission, such as single points of failure, poor scalability, inadequate security, and difficulties in data sharing. First, by analyzing the characteristics of meteorological data and the limitations of existing technologies, the feasibility and advantages of applying blockchain and distributed storage technology in the field of meteorological data are explored. The author designs an overall architecture consisting of a meteorological blockchain data collection layer, blockchain network layer, distributed storage layer, and application service layer. The functions and implementation methods of core components, such as the data collection module, blockchain module, distributed storage module, and data access module, are elaborated in detail. A blockchain-based distributed storage and networking system for meteorological data is constructed. Through experiments and result analysis, the proposed solution is shown to improve data processing efficiency by over 30%, while ensuring data security and access speed, greatly enhancing the meteorological digital infrastructure's support capability for forecasting and disaster prevention and mitigation services.

articleTitle: Research on Random Number Prediction and Security Threats in Embedded Linux Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Linux is one of the most popular open source operating systems, which has the characteristics of small size, strong stability, high portability and wide support for hardware. It is widely used in key network equipment such as routers, switches, firewalls and various intelligent home appliances of Internet of things. By analyzing the kernel code of a specific version of Linux, researchers have discovered the kernel random number vulnerability of Linux system running on a certain type of device. The vulnerability greatly reduces the variable space of entropy source in the initialization process of random entropy pool in the system kernel. So as to realize the prediction of all the random numbers in the whole operation cycle of the system. The use of predictive random number methods can cause serious security problems to the critical services hosted in the system that use random numbers as related keys or authentication means.

articleTitle: Low Speed Sensorless Control of BLDCM Based on High Frequency Signal Coupling Injection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low detection accuracy, poor load capacity and large noise in the existing position sensorless control method when the brushless DC motor is running at low speed, this paper proposes a method of brushless DC motor low-speed sensorless control based on Buck-Boost converter and high-frequency signal coupling injection. This method uses an external high-frequency signal source to send out low-voltage and high-frequency detection signals, which are injected into the motor windings through the coupling circuit and the drive voltage output by the inverter at the same time, and the rotor position is determined by collecting the high-frequency voltage information fed back from the motor windings. The method proposed in this paper is simple and can improve the position detection accuracy and load capacity of the motor at low speed, and reduce the motor noise caused by the detection pulse. The simulation results verify the correctness of the theory and the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Research on Network Attack Monitoring Based on Application HTTP Traffic Parameter Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Currently, enterprise web application security monitoring predominantly relies on devices such as Web Application Firewalls (WAF) and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS). However, these tools often struggle to detect targeted penetration and business logic attacks. This paper introduces a novel security monitoring technology that analyzes session parameter characteristics of web applications. By extracting access parameters, our method establishes six key features: parameter name, fixed-class parameter value, parameter value length, parameter value type, parameter request frequency within a single session, and user-binding class parameter value. A baseline model is then created through feature learning of normal sessions, allowing for effective identification of penetration attacks that deviate from typical session patterns. Testing on real enterprise web application session logs demonstrates that this method achieves a false alarm rate of 0.18% and an accuracy of 99.77%. It effectively monitors penetration attacks that traditional security devices often miss, thereby compensating for their limitations and offering significant practical application value.

articleTitle: Study on an Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm for UAV Image-Based Road Crack Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted road crack detection is a key technology in modern road maintenance, which can effectively reduce the labor costs and improve the recognition efficiency compared to traditional detection methods. This study addresses the issues existing in current road crack detection methods and proposes an improved YOLOv8 model-based automatic recognition algorithm, YOLOv8-D-CBAM, suitable for high-resolution images collected by UAVs. Firstly, to more flexibly obtain crack information from the UAV perspective and enhance the recognition rate, we introduce depthwise separable convolutions into the backbone network of the model to improve its adaptability to complex scenes. Secondly, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is added to the neck of the model to further enhance the feature extraction capability in UAV images. With these improvements, our algorithm significantly increases the recognition rate of road cracks and the model’s performance. Experimental results show that the YOLOv8-D-CBAM algorithm achieves precision, recall, F1-score, and mAP@0.5 of 98.21%, 98.21%, 97.9%, and 99.5%, respectively, on images collected by UAVs, with recognition rates for various crack diseases exceeding 90%. Therefore, the YOLOv8-D-CBAM algorithm demonstrates excellent model performance in the research of UAV-assisted road crack recognition.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Formation Control with Size Scaling for Polyhedral Structures Based on Local Angular and Distance Information
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: This paper investigates the group control problem of multi-agent systems in three-dimensional space, aiming to achieve the formation task of polyhedral shapes through local angular and distance constraints, and to navigate around obstacles and through narrow spaces using scale scaling control. The configuration method of using the first three agents to form a triangular basic framework and then applying vertex addition to complete the formation of the remaining agents is discussed. In this approach, the measured angular information of the agents maintains the angular rigidity of the entire formation, ensuring the uniqueness of the formation shape. By measuring distance information through only one agent, the size of the entire formation is also uniquely determined. Additionally, a configuration method is proposed in which the first four agents form a rectangular basic framework, followed by vertex addition to complete the formation of the remaining agents. This method also ensures angular rigidity, and the inclusion of distance measurements uniquely determines the size of the entire formation. Finally, using a simplified model of Quadrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (QUAVs), simulation experiments demonstrate the formation’s ability to flexibly change its size when encountering obstacles and to pass through narrow spaces, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed formation scheme.

articleTitle: Research on the Continuous Operation Mechanism of Medium and Long Term Electricity Trading Based on Standard Contracts
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: At present, China's electricity market reform has entered a deep water zone, and the electricity market system is constantly improving. As an important part of the complete electricity market system, long-term electricity trading urgently needs further refinement in terms of trading cycle, trading granularity, and other aspects. It is necessary to promote the transformation of medium and long-term electricity trading from "total electricity quantity and electricity price" trading to "segmented electricity quantity and electricity price" trading through market-oriented means, which can effectively connect with the electricity spot market. In view of this, this article proposes a monthly continuous operation mechanism based on medium and long-term electricity trading. By establishing electricity standardization contracts, energy trading and contract trading are integrated. Based on this, the securities market trading model is borrowed to construct a medium and long-term continuous rolling consolidation trading model for electricity. Finally, typical provinces were selected to verify the effectiveness of the mechanism and model proposed in this paper. It can effectively stimulate market vitality and competitiveness, laying the foundation for the orderly connection between the medium and long-term electricity market and the spot market.

Author Keywords: continuous market opening within the month
Integrated trading of electricity energy and contracts

articleTitle: Visual Servoing under Limited Field of View (FOV) for Lumbar Vertebrae Positioning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: X-ray machines are vital in medical imaging for viewing internal body structures. However, in lumbar vertebrae surgery, the X-ray machine has to move and position frequently and manually, which risks infection, misalignment, and overexposure to radiation. There’s a need for mobile X-ray machines with autonomous recognition and positioning. Although visual servoing suitable for X-ray positioning naturally, it still experiencing challenges like limited Field-of-View (FOV) and the structural similarity among vertebrae. In this paper, a Bayesian Estimation based approach is developed to improve the detection accuracy in case of vertebrae positions outside the FOV. Furthermore, a visual servoing method is proposed for X-ray positioning, considering their mechanical structure and imaging characteristics. The experiment results indicates that the proposed approach improves lumbar vertebrae detection accuracy significantly. This approach facilitates precise positioning in X-ray imaging and enhances the safety and effectiveness of lumbar vertebrae surgery.

articleTitle: Game-Theory-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicles in Highway Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles have become a popular topic with the development of technology. In the early stages of an automated driving system, the key to correctly guiding the vehicle’s behavior lies in the effective collection and application of expert driving experience. This study introduces a game-theoretic guided reinforcement learning (GTG-RL) framework that merges game-theoretic expert models with reinforcement learning to enhance decision-making efficiency for autonomous vehicles in complex motorway scenarios. Validation confirms the framework’s effectiveness in improving performance and adaptability under dynamic traffic conditions. The results underscore the potential of integrating game-theoretic expertise with reinforcement learning to tackle autonomous driving challenges.

articleTitle: A Novel Routing Equipment Fault Diagnosis Scheme Based On Machine Learning In Short Distance Communication Scenario
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: In the short distance communication scenario, the stable and efficient operation of routing equipment is very important, but there is no method to achieve high fault identification accuracy. In this paper, a fault diagnosis scheme for routing equipment based on machine learning in short distance communication scenarios is proposed. A generative adversarial network based on quantum state optimization is adopted for data augmentation, a neural network based on locally sensitive honeypot optimization algorithm is adopted to effectively identify and extract key features, and an improved autoencoder is adopted for feature dimension reduction. The classification performance is optimized by support vector machine based on covariate matrix. The experimental results show that this scheme can achieve a high accuracy of fault identification of routing equipment, and has greater deployment and promotion value.

articleTitle: DR Image Enhancement Method for Complex Components Based on Zero-Reference Pixel Mapping Curve
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: DR (Digital Real-Time Imaging) technology has become the preferred method for industrial defect detection due to its fast detection speed and low radiation dose, and the enhancement technology for DR images of complex components will serve as a crucial foundation for ensuring effective defect identification. However, the current manual parameter adjustment method for enhancing DR images often results in inconsistent and inefficient outcomes. Additionally, existing deep learning-based enhancement methods face challenges such as the scarcity of paired datasets or high-quality reference images when applied to industrial DR image enhancement tasks. To solve the above problems, a DR image enhancement method based on zero reference pixel mapping curve is proposed. Firstly, the image pixel feature extraction network (IPFE-Net) was constructed to extract the features of the input image and obtain its pixel feature matrix (MOPF). Then, using MOPF as the parameter matrix, the input low-quality image is iteratively transformed according to the preset pixel transformation function to achieve pixel by pixel nonlinear grayscale mapping. Thirdly, a zero reference image loss function is designed to drive model training and constrain various physical features of the output image to achieve image enhancement. Through validation on actual enterprise datasets, the results indicate that this method effectively enhances the image quality and defect detection performance of DR images for complex components.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation Techniques for Security Threat Levels of Critical Information Assets in Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of power grid information systems and the rapid pace of digital transformation, information security is crucial for maintaining grid stability. This paper proposes a risk assessment method that links hierarchical threats to assets, integrating big data and knowledge graph technologies. It develops a multi-layered security threat model tailored to key power grid assets, capable of identifying and quantifying risks at various network levels in a dynamic environment. This model provides more accurate support for security management and decision-making, reflecting both threat probabilities and potential impacts. It also adapts risk assessments based on different security measures, offering flexibility. The proposed approach is significant for enhancing the security of power grid information systems and offers valuable insights and technical support for future grid security protection.

articleTitle: Empowering Knowledge Management by Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) in Firm-hosted Online Communities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Firm-hosted online communities, as a kind of typical online platform connecting enterprises and users, play an important role in user-related knowledge management. Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) brings about changes in the logic of knowledge production which have a series of impacts on user-related knowledge management in firm-hosted online communities, such as user socialization, brand marketing, user services, and user innovation. Based on the "requirement-function-technology" framework, this paper explores the relationship between the knowledge management requirements and the availability of AIGC, and analyzes the transformation of knowledge management empowered by AIGC in firm-hosted online communities.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction of Command and Control System for Multi Domain Parallel Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: In the era of intelligent warfare, multi domain space warfare consisting of physical domain, in-formation domain, and cognitive domain is the mainstream form. Based on a comprehensive analysis of the development trend of command and control systems, the connotation of the concept of multi domain parallel operations, and the capability requirements of command and control systems, an innovative concept of a command and control system for multi domain parallel operations was proposed. The system architecture, system composition, key technology groups, and deployment strategies of the system were designed, with a particular focus on analyzing technical difficulties and planning implementation paths, in order to provide useful references for the design and development of the new generation of command and control systems.

articleTitle: A Electric Power Scene Object Detection Algorithm Based on Meta-learning and Category Decoupling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: With the large-scale application and practical improvement of intelligent inspection in electric power scene, the ability to identify equipment defects has become increasingly important. Currently, the mainstream algorithms for equipment defect identification primarily rely on established techniques such as YOLO, CenterNet, etc. These algorithms perform exceptionally well on public datasets. However, in terms of the imbalance of class and the conflict between conceptual categories for equipment defect identification tasks, there is still room for optimization in these algorithms. In this work, we propose a YOLO-paradigm algorithm combined with meta-learning, which resolves issues of class imbalance and conceptual conflict between categories by decoupling the categories of detection head and providing categorical instance support through meta-learning. This algorithm is implemented through end-to-end training, and during the inference stage, the weighted coefficients obtained from the meta-learning module are fixed, reducing computational overhead. On the equipment defect dataset we have made, the proposed method in this work demonstrates better performance than the baseline model, especially for categories with few samples.

articleTitle: A Cloud Storage Auditing Scheme Based on Identity-Based Signature
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Cloud storage has become the most widely used medium for data storage. When users upload, delete, or modify data in the cloud, ensuring data integrity and semantic correctness is a critical challenge. Existing solutions rely on a data verification engine to validate dynamic data operations and use hash-based schemes to ensure data integrity. However, these approaches often allow data auditors to access the audited data, leading to potential privacy breaches and making them unsuitable for real-time applications. To address this issue, we propose an efficient data auditing solution that leverages the RSA signature and a provable data possession (PDP) scheme to verify cloud data. This approach enhances data privacy and significantly reduces bandwidth consumption compared to hash-based methods. Security analysis confirms that the proposed solution ensures audit soundness, while experimental results demonstrate its high execution efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Maglev Variable Stiffness Joints for A Wide Range of Stiffness and Angle Changes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: To address the current issues of traditional variable stiffness joints, such as limited motion range, large overall dimensions, and significant energy loss, this paper proposes a novel maglev variable stiffness joint that further enhances the safety and energy efficiency of human-robot interaction. This joint combines the trigonometric relationships within a triangular structure and the exponential growth trend of the repulsive force of magnetic materials, better simulating the nonlinear characteristics of the human elbow joint to achieve a wide range of stiffness and angle variations. At the same time, a static and dynamic analysis of the maglev variable stiffness joint is conducted. A static model is established through geometric and mechanical analysis, and a dynamic model is built based on Lagrange’s equations and the principle of virtual work, resolving the complexity issues in modeling and control of traditional variable stiffness joints and providing a new method for the control of flexible robotic arm joints.

articleTitle: Design of a Lightweight Privacy Communication Network System for Medium Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Medium and large enterprises need to exchange confidential information frequently. Traditional encryption techniques can only protect the security of communication data, but the privacy of the communicating entities' identity information cannot be effectively protected. Currently, common solutions include virtual private networks (VPNs) and single/multiple agent-based forwarding mechanisms. However, the egress nodes of VPNs are susceptible to attacks and monitoring; agents in single-agent forwarding mechanisms are easy targets for single points of failure and attacks. Medium and large enterprises urgently need a solution that ensures communication privacy while being cost-effective and easy to manage. Therefore, this paper proposes a lightweight privacy communication network system based on a multi-agent mechanism to realize the non-association of communication parties and provide transparent transmission services. In order to schedule and manage the whole system flexibly, this paper implements a remote service and a visualization service in a Directory Server. In addition, an intelligent multi-objective optimization analysis of the route selection algorithm is introduced to ensure the anti-tracking and high efficiency of data transmission; meanwhile, traffic obfuscation technology is used to prevent attackers from recognizing the communication content and the identities of both parties through the traffic pattern, which improves the transmission and management security of the system. Test results show that the system effectively protects information communication relationships in medium and large enterprises.

articleTitle: A Study on Short-Term Nowcasting Precipitation Forecasting Methods Based on Radar Echo Maps
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Short-To-medium-term precipitation nowcasting aims to predict changes in mesoscale and microscale weather systems, particularly severe convective systems, within 0 to 2 hours. Compared to large-scale weather systems, mesoscale and microscale systems are characterized by their abruptness, complex mechanisms, and short life cycles, making short-term precipitation forecasting a highly challenging field. This study focuses on the Yinchuan region as a case study, processing radar echo data through dimensionality reduction, noise reduction, frame interpolation, and data augmentation to construct datasets suitable for training and testing. The IAM4VPx5 model is employed for forecasting and is compared against traditional spatiotemporal prediction models, including SimVP, ConvLSTM, and ConvGRU. Experimental results demonstrate that the IAM4VPx5 model outperforms SimVP, ConvLSTM, and ConvGRU across multiple metrics, such as Critical Success Index (CSI), Heidke Skill Score (HSS), and Probability of Detection (POD). Additionally, IAM4VPx5 exhibits superior performance in Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). Overall, the IAM4VPx5 model demonstrates exceptional performance compared to SimVP, ConvLSTM, and ConvGRU in various aspects. These results validate the effectiveness and advantages of the IAM4VPx5 model in processing radar echo data, offering an efficient solution for weather radar forecasting.

articleTitle: Development of Poisson's Ratio Measurement Software Based on Digital Twin Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an innovative software tool that utilizes digital twin technology to measure the Poisson's ratio. Traditional measurement methods often face challenges due to the small magnitude of axial and radial strains, leading to inaccuracies and insufficient data representation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a digital twin-based approach that enables the creation of a virtual replica of physical systems, allowing for real-time simulation and analysis of material behavior. This software not only facilitates precise measurement of the Poisson's ratio but also generates interactive visual representations of the data, thereby enhancing the understanding of engineers and stakeholders. Our research findings indicate that integrating digital twin technology into Poisson's ratio testing is not only feasible but also beneficial. This approach significantly improves measurement reliability and showcases visually enriched plots, making it easier for engineers and researchers to interpret complex data. The utilization of digital twins allows for real-time simulations and comprehensive data analysis, which are crucial for understanding material behavior under external loads.

articleTitle: The Item Category-Oriented User Behavior Path Analysis in CTR Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: In E-commerce, Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction models are often intended for analyzing user behavior patterns, identifying potential user interests, and therefore estimating purchasing intent. Existing models often incorporate various types of interactions between users and items/products (referred to as multi-type user behavior) to address the issue of data sparsity caused by relying on a single type of behavior. While this method introduces more user behavior features, it also brings some irrelevant noise into the prediction model—information not directly related to the predicted item. To address this, we introduce the concept of the Item Category-oriented User behavior Path, or ICUP, which consist of behaviors such as clicks, add-to-cart actions, and favorites, all focused on items within the same category. These behavior paths not only reflect the user’s potential interest in the target category of items but also implicitly indicate the user’s thought processes and decision-making throughout the purchasing process. We employ an adaptive mechanism for depicting the unique characteristics of user behavior preferences. Finally, a contrastive learning mechanism is integrated into the feature representation of behavior paths, enhancing the accuracy of the feature representation. We conducted a series of experiments on the publicly available Taobao dataset, and the results verify that our CTR prediction method yields desirable improvements in AUC and accuracy compared to baseline models.

articleTitle: Distributed Fusion for Satellite Orbit Determination with Angles-only Measurements
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: This paper studies the distributed state estimation problem for noncooperative targets with angles-only measurements. We first establish the angles-only observation model of satellite formation and use the extended Kalman filter to obtain the states of noncooperative targets. To address the mild assumption on communication topology and local observability, a peer-to-peer distributed fusion is introduced, wherein each satellite interacts with its interconnected peers to attain consensus on weighted measurements and inverse-covariance matrices. Then, to reduce the error of the dynamic consensus algorithm, a consensus approach is introduced to unify the estimation results of each satellite. Moreover, the stability and convergence of the distributed Kalman Filtering are examined. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed estimation approach has better performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Distributed Energy Storage Configuration to Improve Power Supply Capacity of Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Energy storage has bidirectional adjustable characteristics, which play an important role in the new power system. First, it can smooth the fluctuation of renewable energy generation. Second, it can provide frequency regulation services. Third, it can provide a backup power supply service to improve the reliability of the power system. Fourth, it can be used for the demand response of the power system to optimize the load curve of the power system using peak shifting, valley filling, and off- peak power consumption. Distributed energy storage multiaccess medium and low voltage distribution network or user side. This paper follows the principles of operability, practicality, science, comparability, reliability, and comprehensiveness. A comprehensive distributed energy storage configuration evaluation index system is established from seven aspects: device level, operation security, power grid reliability, power supply quality, peak cutting and valley filling effect, consumption capacity, and economy of distributed power supply. The overall scoring and implementation effect of distributed energy storage is objectively evaluated by using an analytic hierarchy process. Finally, the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed algorithm are verified by a practical distribution network.

articleTitle: Research on the Value Evaluation Technology of Big Data Assets in Power Grid Dispatching and Control
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: In response to the current issue of rough management and operation methods for power grid dispatching and control data, this article takes the regulation data object as the core, integrates electrical physical characteristics, time polymorphism characteristics, multi-source information characteristics, and business implications of data asset planning methods, and proposes a multi domain value evaluation technology research that considers data ontology attributes and power grid operation mechanisms.. Firstly, conduct a comprehensive and in-depth analysis of the deep-seated characteristics, laws, and mechanisms of power grid regulation data, and establish an element system for evaluating the asset value of power grid regulation data; Secondly, use Analytic Hierarchy Process and Expert Scoring to construct a valuation model for regulatory data assets; Finally, the feasibility and rationality of the data asset value evaluation method are verified through typical power regulation data application scenarios. The validation results indicate that the proposed regulatory data asset evaluation method can quantify the value evaluation of regulatory data assets, improve the data management capability and scheduling lean management level of regulatory big data platforms.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Bidding Strategy of New Energy Power Station with Energy Storage Considering the Uncertainty of Wind and Solar Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: With the proposal of dual-carbon target, the new power system presents the characteristic of high proportion of new energy penetration, and the volatility and uncertainty of new energy bring challenges to the stability and reliability of the energy system supply and demand, and at the same time is not conducive to the new energy as an independent subject of the market-oriented competition. Through the new energy distribution storage, in the form of joint participation in the day-ahead market for clearing, using stochastic optimization method to construct new energy output scenarios, day-ahead and real-time clearing tariff scenarios, using K-medoids method for the reduction of the typical scenarios, to new energy distribution storage power station system of the day-ahead revenue maximum as the goal, the establishment of the new energy joint energy storage to participate in the day-ahead market bidding strategy model. Finally, based on the historical data of a new energy power station and the spot market tariff data for example analysis, the results verify the effectiveness of the bidding strategy model.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Evaluation and Analysis Framework of Command Information System Resilience based on Complex Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Focusing on the key issues such as the construction of structural model, the establishment of resilience index system, and the analysis of resilience evaluation, this paper provides a descriptive definition of command information system resilience based on an in-depth analysis of the concept and process of resilience. Combined with the military characteristics and functional attributes of the system, it summarizes what should be focused on in evaluation of command information system resilience. A dynamic evaluation and analysis framework for command information system resilience based on complex networks is proposed, utilizing the unique advantages of complex network theory in describing the static structural characteristics and dynamic behavioral characteristics. The framework covers six core aspects, including uncertainty analysis, system structure modeling, index system construction, evaluation experiment design, simulation experiment system and model construction, experimental verification and evaluation analysis. It comprehensively and systematically integrates the key elements of resilience evaluation, and forms a complete dynamic process, which not only provides powerful direction and framework foundation for the construction of command information system resilience theoretical system, but also offers valuable references for system resilience design and optimization.

articleTitle: An Improved Seagull Optimization Algorithm for Multi-Center Maintenance Task Allocation of UAV Swarm Under Resource Constraints
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: This paper addresses the optimization problem of maintenance and support task allocation and scheduling for unmanned aerial vehicle (UA V) swarms when performing multi - batch continuous sortie missions. Against the backdrop of multiple maintenance centers, multiple maintenance personnel, and multiple equipment spare parts, a maintenance and support task allocation method based on the improved seagull optimization algorithm is studied. Under the condition of limited maintenance resources, this algorithm aims to minimize the batch sortie preparation time, optimize the workload balance of maintenance personnel, and minimize the total maintenance and support time of the UA V swarm. By introducing chaos mapping, non - linear additional variables, greedy insertion, Levy flight, and random multi - point exchange strategies into the seagull optimization algorithm, the optimization of the maintenance and support task allocation scheme is achieved. Through experiments with background case data, compared with traditional algorithms, the improved seagull algorithm proposed in this paper has significantly improved in optimization indicators such as the sortie time of the next task, task balance, and total maintenance and support time.

articleTitle: Recognition and Traffic Warning of Severe Weather using Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Severe weather has a significant impact on road traffic operations, safety, and autonomous driving, making it susceptible to serious accidents due to drivers' erroneous perceptions of the environment and inappropriate driving speeds. To prevent and reduce traffic accidents in severe weather conditions, providing accurate speed warning information is essential for ensuring the safe operation of motor vehicles on highways under adverse weather conditions. Firstly, based on severe weather image data, different levels of severe weather are categorized according to traffic meteorological condition classification standards. Through the integration of deep neural network theories, an automatic monitoring model is established to identify the captured video frame information from highway surveillance. Secondly, based on the driving safety speed model, visibility, rainfall intensity, road surface friction coefficient, and other indicators are combined to design a safety speed limit warning system. Finally, a severe weather recognition and warning system along with a visualization tool are designed and deployed on the Web platform. The practical results demonstrate that the Resnet50 recognition model based on severe weather images exhibits good data adaptability and accurate identification results in sunny, rainy, foggy, and mixed datasets.

articleTitle: Study on transaction mechanism and settlement method for large-scale participation of virtual power plant
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: This paper aims to explore the mechanism and settlement method of large-scale participation of virtual power plantsin electricity market trading. As a new mode of power resource aggregation and optimal scheduling,virtual power plant can improve energy utilization efficiency and market responsiveness by integrating distributed energyresources, fully stimulate virtual power plant's multi-time scale (medium and long term,spot) power and corresponding safety regulation capacity by market means through the design of trading mechanism suitable forlarge-scale participation, and the corresponding settlement method. However,virtual power plants are also faced with market problems such as tight supply and demand and weak power grid regulationability, which require emerging market entities to stimulate value,but lack a trading mechanism and settlement method that takes into account the corresponding output and regulatorycharacteristics of virtual power plants. In view of this,this paper proposes a trading mechanism an d settlement method that ADAPTS to the large-scale participation of virtual powerplants.

articleTitle: Multi-head self-attentive GRU-based missing data repair method for wind turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Due to temporary anomalies in sensor readings and additional issues, the data collected by wind turbine monitoring and control systems often feature a considerable number of missing values. This can have detrimental impacts on various critical aspects such as wind power prediction, the calculation of wind power curves, and the implementation of necessary corrections. Traditional approaches to missing data repair in wind turbine datasets rely mainly on machine learning and deep learning techniques. However, methods based on traditional machine learning are often limited by their shallow architectures, which restricts their ability to deeply explore and understand complex data features. On the other hand, while deep learning methods can capture intricate patterns in data, they frequently overlook the temporal dependencies inherent in time-series data. To address these significant challenges and effectively uncover the temporal correlations among the dataset's features, this paper proposes a novel approach for repairing missing data in wind turbines utilizing a multi-head self-attention mechanism within a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) framework. The proposed methodology begins with normalizing the dataset and subsequently dividing it into training and testing subsets. Key feature parameters are selected based on the Pearson correlation coefficient to ensure that only the most relevant data is utilized. The core of the approach lies in constructing a GRU model augmented with a multi-head self-attention mechanism, allowing for the restoration of data with proportionate and continuous missing values. Results obtained from the experiments demonstrate that the proposed method not only effectively fills in the missing data but also adequately learns the variation patterns of feature parameters, outperforming traditional GRU and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithms in accurately repairing multi-dimensional parameter data.

articleTitle: BGatCCN: A sentiment analysis network based on BERT utilizing graph attention and dynamic conditional parameter convolution
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is an essential direction in natural language processing. Previous studies often classified text without fully considering the overall sentiment of the text. To address these issues, we propose a new model that utilizes BERT, a conditional parameter convolutional network, and a graph attention network. Our approach uses hidden state information from the last four layers of BERT. The information is converted into a graph attention matrix through the graph attention layer, which then undergoes conditional parameter convolutions to generate text feature vectors. Max pooling is used to capture the most relevant features for each moment. These features are then combined to obtain global feature information. Finally, we perform sentiment analysis using linear mapping. Through experiments, our model achieves better results on datasets.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Multiple Machine Learning Algorithms in Heart Disease Classification Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: This paper aims to evaluate the effectiveness of various machine learning models in handling classification tasks by comparing and analyzing their performance on two different datasets. The study employs multiple machine learning models, including Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron, K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBoost, Support Vector Machines, AdaBoost, Logistic Regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Linear Discriminant Analysis, Decision Trees, and Gradient Boosting. For each model, metrics such as accuracy, precision, F1 score, log loss, Hamming loss, and Jaccard similarity coefficient are calculated on both datasets D1 and D2. Additionally, the performance of the models is further analyzed through Precision-Recall (PR) curves and Area Under the Curve (AUC) curves. On dataset D1, XGBoost, AdaBoost, Logistic Regression, and Gradient Boosting models exhibit outstanding performance in accuracy. The Multi-Layer Perceptron achieves the best precision and Jaccard similarity coefficient, while the Gradient Boosting model performs the best in log loss and Hamming loss. For dataset D2, Logistic Regression obtains the highest values in multiple evaluation metrics, demonstrating its superiority in handling this dataset. Ensemble learning methods show good performance on both datasets, while linear models are notable for their efficiency and interpretability. Ensemble learning methods and linear models exhibit excellent performance in handling classification tasks, especially on complex datasets. Different datasets have significant impacts on model performance, and selecting an appropriate model requires comprehensive consideration of dataset characteristics and task requirements. Future research can further explore new evaluation metrics and methods, as well as cross-domain data fusion and model transfer, to enhance the generalization ability and practicality of machine learning models.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Teaching System for College English Listening and Speaking Course Empowered by Generative Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: To explore the practical application effects of generative artificial intelligence in college English listening and speaking course, this study designed and implemented a teaching system comprising four main modules: teaching content management, interactive learning, assessment and feedback, and user management and interaction. Leveraging advanced technologies such as automatic speech recognition, natural language processing, and Long Short-Term Memory networks, the system fully meets the needs of English listening and speaking course. Test results show that compared to traditional systems, this system has significant advantages in indexes including English listening and speaking test scores, speech pronunciation accuracy, and language fluency. According to research findings, there exists potential of generative artificial intelligence in enhancing teaching efficiency and quality in college English listening and speaking courses.

articleTitle: Value Analysis of Load Side Resource Flexibility in a New Power Load Management System Based on Value Concepts
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: With the gradual formation and development of a new type of power system dominated by new energy, the power grid is facing the risk of insufficient regulation capacity, and load side resources can provide flexibility for the power system at multiple time scales. Firstly, the definition of power system flexibility is introduced, and then the flexibility supply-demand balance of transmission and distribution networks at different time scales under the background of the new power system is discussed. Taking three types of load side resources with development potential, namely temperature controlled loads, electric vehicles, and load side hydrogen energy hubs, as research objects, the flexibility value and feasibility of demand side support for the flexibility demand of the new power system were analyzed.

articleTitle: Research on the Method of Redundant Force Suppression for Aircraft Active Side Sticks Based on Adaptive Robust Control
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: The problem of redundant force present in the system resulting from the pilot's manipulation of the active side stick may give rise to poor postural perception, which in turn affects the handling quality. It should be noted that the redundant force can only be mitigated rather than eradicated. In order to suppress the redundant force, this paper elaborates on a variety of control strategies, proposes an adaptive robust control approach, establishes a system model, designs a robust controller, and carries out stability analysis. Through experimental verification, the control performances of PID and adaptive robust control on both linear and nonlinear rod-force curves under different speeds are investigated. The results demonstrate that adaptive robust control enhances the force control accuracy by approximately 60% compared to PID, and exhibits superior error stability.

articleTitle: Estimating Combustible Load and Fire Risk in Zhejiang Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: The power grid system is a cornerstone of modern socio-economic development and is crucial for the stable operation of Zhejiang Province, an economically prosperous region. This study tackles the fire risk management challenges in the province ’ s transmission corridors by utilizing remote sensing technology and machine learning algorithms. Specifically, it develops methods for estimating combustible material loads and assessing fire risks. Using high-resolution optical imagery, hyperspectral data, and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, along with ground plot surveys, we extracted spectral characteristics, texture features, and structural information from vegetation to create accurate models for tree species classification and combustible material load estimation. This led to the creation of a combustible material distribution map for the transmission corridors throughout the province. In parallel, we integrated meteorological data and regional phenological characteristics to develop a dynamic fire risk assessment model, which resulted in the generation of fire risk level distribution maps. This research significantly improves the accuracy of vegetation monitoring and fire risk assessment in transmission corridors, providing optimized tools for safe power grid management and enhancing inspection and early warning systems. The findings offer a scientific foundation for forest fire prevention and ecological protection strategies, with wide potential for application and dissemination.

articleTitle: Full-real-life Wind Power Prediction based on Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Wind energy is highly random, volatile and uncontrollable. Therefore, in order to ensure the reliable and efficient operation of wind farm power generation connected to the grid in a full-real-life environment, accurate wind power prediction based on weather forecasts is crucial. This paper uses a learning algorithm based on a gradient boosting decision tree (XGBoost algorithm and LightGBM algorithm) to develop two models to study the power prediction effect in a full-real-life environment. Both models are trained using ECMWF weather forecast data and 19 months of wind farm power generation. Preliminary experiments show that the XGBoost algorithm is slightly better than the LightGBM algorithm in terms of accuracy, but the LightGBM algorithm is much shorter than the XGBoost algorithm in terms of training time. Since data is updated frequently in a full-real- life scenario and the model training time requirement is short, a model based on the LightGBM algorithm is selected to verify the power prediction effect of a wind farm in a full- real-life environment. In a full-real-life environment, the ECMWF weather forecast is input into the LightGBM model to perform ultra-short-term, short-term and medium-term forecasts on wind farm power. The full-real-life evaluation standard adopts the industry grid-connected rules. The simulation results of the full-real-life environment confirm that the learning algorithm based on the gradient boosting decision tree can not only be used for ultra-short-term, shortterm and medium-term wind farm power forecasting, but also has excellent prediction results in the ultra-short-term and short-term. At the same time, more accurate weather forecasts are more important for power forecasting.

articleTitle: Construction of Ghost Imaging LiDAR System Based on Dual Fast Mirrors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Influenced by factors such as system bandwidth, rotational inertia, and tracking range in the GI LiDAR system, reliance on a large inertia tracking mechanism alone is challenging. Conversely, a small inertia tracking system may struggle to satisfy the system’s operational range needs. A composite axis control system is formed by combining a large inertia tracking system with a small inertia one to fulfill the tracking accuracy demands. In order to enhance the receiving aperture of the GI LiDAR system, this paper introduces a GI LiDAR system based on dual fast mirrors. Furthermore, a high-precision composite axis PAT control method is introduced to address the motion blur issue with the framework of the dual fast mirrors-based GI LiDAR system.

articleTitle: High-Voltage GIS Devices Fault Diagnosis Leveraging Sequence-to-Sequence Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: The real-time fault diagnosis of High Voltage Gas Insulated Switches (HV-GIS) is critical for maintaining the safety and operational reliability of electrical grids. Conventional diagnostic techniques mainly depend on statistical feature extraction followed by machine learning-based classification. However, these methods often face challenges in effectively handling the complexities introduced by varying aging processes and diverse operating conditions. In order to address the issues, we introduce a general fault diagnosis framework for HV-GIS that leverages sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) modeling. Our framework transforms sensing data into sequences and treats the diagnosis task as a seq2seq problem, leveraging this modeling approach to achieve a generalized fault diagnosis. Experimental results indicate that the diagnosis model trained with our framework outperforms baseline models, offering a more effective and generalized solution for HV-GIS fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact Mechanism of Synergetic Cyber Attacks on Electric Cyber Physical System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: With the development of modern communication technology, the integration of the power system and the electric information network is becoming closer and closer, which results in a united electric cyber physical system (ECPS). The ECPS can achieve functions such as rapid fault detection and optimal power flow management through advanced information analysis and decision-making processes. Furthermore, in the event of an attack on the electric information network, the physical power system may become vulnerable to catastrophic failures. For instance, in 2015, a large-scale blackout occurred in the Ukrainian power grid that lasted for several hours, due to cyber attacks on multiple 220kV substations. And in 2019, the Guli Hydropower Station, which accounts for 40% of Venezuela's electricity generation, and the corresponding control center were suffered from cyber attacks, resulting in a major blackout that affects 18 states in this country. In this paper, we define a synergetic cyber attack as an orchestrated assault targeting multiple cyber nodes that correspond to critical physical nodes. As demonstrated by the aforementioned events, synergetic cyber attacks have the potential to pose a significant threat to the security of ECPS. Therefore, summarizing the characteristics of current information physical security incidents and analyzing the impact mechanisms of synergistic cyber attacks on ECPS hold significant practical importance.

articleTitle: Wireless Continuous Monitoring System for Biological Parameters in Infant Incubator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: High mortality rates faced by preterm infants in resource-limited settings are often due to common issues arising without prompt medical intervention, including reduced oxygen levels, improper temperature and humidity regulation in incubators, and undetected changes in vital signs like heart rate. This study aimed to design a system that continuously tracks critical measurements such as infant temperature, pulse rate, and incubator humidity levels, sending real-time data via mobile networks to parents and clinicians for prompt response. Sensors were installed in incubators across three hospitals to monitor parameters from preterm babies. Data was wirelessly transmitted via Wi-Fi to a central computer for analysis, which checked for measurement anomalies and created alerts to notify the care team when issues were detected. An early version of the system was tested, successfully collecting all necessary health data without disruptions for over 48 hours and maintaining stable wireless connectivity. This method proved superior to previous manual checks. Initial results indicate that this monitoring approach could significantly reduce mortality rates in resource-limited hospitals by identifying previously overlooked problems.

articleTitle: OpenCV-based Recognition Method for Computer Interlocking Host Computer Interface
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of identifying the operation of computer interlocking host computer interface and promote the improvement of automation, combined with the display standards and requirements of the host computer interface, this paper proposes an image analysis method for the host computer interface based on Open CV. The method accurately extracts the coordinate information on the screen by quantifying the geometric features of various types of signal devices in the host computer interface. Through this process, it can realise the automatic identification, obtain the whole station's signal layout map from the image input, and make preparations for the subsequent automated test.

articleTitle: Fusing multi-model features for malware classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: Over the past few decades, many malware classification methods have emerged. Methods based on machine learning rely on manually extracted features, while those based on deep learning can reduce manual intervention and improve model generalization capabilities. However, these methods mostly characterize malicious code as a single type of feature, with a single source and form of features, resulting in poor performance compared to multimodal methods. In this work, we propose FuMalk, which combines three data modalities: (1) opcode calls statistically derived from malicious code assembly files, (2) grayscale images representing malicious code, and (3) control flow graphs extracted from malicious code assembly files. Fu-Malk characterizes malicious code as multi-modal features, fully utilizing the complementary characteristics of different forms of features. This paper uses ten-fold cross-validation to evaluate the proposed method, and the experimental results show that FuMalk achieves an average accuracy of 99.77% on Microsoft’s public dataset.

articleTitle: Cooperatively Localizing Multi-Target by Dynamic UAV Formation Equipped with Bearing-only Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 8th Information Technology and Mechatronics Engineering Conference (ITOEC)
abstract: In recent years, the applications of UAV swarm equipped with electro-optical pods have become increasingly widespread. Electro-optical pods are passive sensors that can only measure bearing, but not distance. In practical scenarios of UAV swarm continuous tracking of multiple targets, the time-sensitive moving targets may move out of or suddenly into the field of view of UAV. Collaboratively localizing multiple time-sensitive targets based on bearing-only measurements is a significant challenge for UAV swarm. Traditional direction-finding cross location methods have significant errors under noisy conditions. Existing target location algorithms based on filtering require fixed UAV formation to track specific target, making them unsuitable for dynamic formations. In this paper, we model the target motion with a constant velocity and linearize the process of UAV swarm observing the positions of targets. Then we use the Extended Kalman Filter to estimate the position of targets based on the above target motion model and linearized observation model. The observation model allows for changes of the UAV formation tracking a specific target. Emulation experiments in the VICON environment and simulation experiments in the AirSim environment validate the applicability and accuracy of this method in scenarios of dynamic UAV formation cooperatively localizing multiple targets.
